method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Start the 75g basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Peel and finely slice the 90g onion and deseed and thinly slice the 90g mixed peppers. Check the 150g salmon fillet for bones. Keep it as a fillet for pan cooking, then flake it after cooking.
Mix 20g light mayonnaise, 5ml lemon juice and 1g dried parsley in a small bowl. Keep this dressing cold until serving; it is not a cooking sauce and must not be simmered in the pan.

Heat half the listed olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Put in the salmon fillet, skin-side down if it has skin. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turn carefully and cook for another 3–5 minutes until the centre is opaque, steaming hot and flakes easily; a thicker piece needs longer. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Add the remaining half of the listed olive oil to the same pan. Add 90g onion and 90g mixed peppers and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until softened with some bite. Keep the heat moderate so the small measured amount of oil does not smoke.

Flake the cooked salmon into large pieces and fold into the pan at the end; avoid breaking it up with vigorous stirring. Heat gently until the whole pan is steaming hot, folding carefully so the seafood stays intact. Spoon the pan mixture over the freshly cooked rice. Take the pan off the heat and spoon the cold dressing over each serving; do not return it to the hob. Serve immediately.
